questions.q: How is bond order (b.o.) defined?
options: It is the sum of electrons in bonding and antibonding orbitals.
It is the difference between the numbers of electrons in bonding and antibonding orbitals.
It is the ratio of electrons in bonding to antibonding orbitals.
It is the average energy of bonding and antibonding orbitals.

questions.q: How many unpaired electrons are there in the ground state electronic configuration of carbon?
questions.solution: The ground state electronic configuration of carbon [He]2s2 2p2 indicates two unpaired electrons.

questions.q: How are atomic orbitals expressed in wave mechanics?
questions.solution: The atomic orbitals can be expressed by wave functions (ψ ’s) in wave mechanics.

questions.q: What is the result of the electronegativity difference between the two atoms in a polar covalent bond?
questions.solution: In a polar covalent bond, the result of the electronegativity difference between the two atoms is that the bond becomes polar covalent.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: What is the condition for a molecule to be stable?
options: N<sub>b</sub> must be less than N<sub>a</sub>
N<sub>b</sub> must be equal to N<sub>a</sub>
The number of electrons doesn't matter for stability
questions.solution: A molecule is stable if the number of electrons occupying bonding orbitals (N<sub>b</sub>) is greater than the number occupying antibonding orbitals (N<sub>a</sub>).

questions.q: What is the result of the electron density distribution in an antibonding molecular orbital?

questions.q: What is the significance of having orbitals with almost equal energy for hybridisation?
options: It allows for the formation of stable compounds.
It determines the type of atom involved in bonding.
It facilitates the promotion of electrons.

questions.q: Which type of force arises between the electrons of two atoms?
questions.solution: The repulsive forces arise between the nuclei of two atoms.

questions.q: How are stability and bond order related?
options: A positive bond order indicates an unstable molecule.
A negative bond order indicates a stable molecule.
A positive bond order indicates a stable molecule.
Bond order is unrelated to the stability of a molecule.
questions.solution: A positive bond order (N<sub>b</sub> > N<sub>a</sub>) signifies a stable molecule.

questions.q: What type of bond is formed when hydrogen is attached to a highly electronegative atom like nitrogen, oxygen, or fluorine?
questions.solution: When hydrogen is attached to a highly electronegative atom like nitrogen, oxygen, or fluorine, a bond known as a hydrogen bond is formed.

options: Because these techniques are more accurate than other methods
Because they allow for the measurement of bond lengths in gaseous samples
Because they provide information about the bond's stability
Because they provide detailed information about the arrangement of atoms in a molecule
questions.solution: These techniques are used because they provide detailed information about the arrangement of atoms in a molecule, which includes bond lengths.

questions.q: What molecular orbital has a node between the nuclei?

questions.q: What is the bond enthalpy of the H – H bond in a hydrogen molecule?
questions.solution: The value of the H – H bond enthalpy in a hydrogen molecule as 435.8 kJ mol-1.

questions.q: Which theory is used to describe the overlap and hybridization of atomic orbitals in polyatomic molecules?
questions.solution: The valence bond theory is used to explain overlap and hybridization of atomic orbitals in polyatomic molecules.

questions.q: What condition must be met by orbitals when they are forming a bond?
options: They should have the same sign (phase) and orientation in space

questions.q: How is the net charge of polyatomic ions typically assigned?
options: To a specific atom within the ion
To the atom with the highest electronegativity
To the ion as a whole
To the least electronegative atom within the ion
questions.solution: In the case of polyatomic ions, the net charge is possessed by the ion as a whole.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: What is the shape of the valence shell assumed to be in the VSEPR theory?
questions.solution: In the VSEPR theory, the valence shell is taken as a sphere, with the electron pairs localizing on the spherical surface at the maximum distance from one another.

questions.q: How do sodium and chlorine achieve a stable octet of electrons, according to Lewis?
questions.solution: In the case of sodium and chlorine, Lewis describes the achievement of a stable octet by the transfer of an electron from sodium to chlorine, forming Na+ and Cl- ions.

questions.q: What happens in the excited state of a Be atom to account for its bivalency?
options: One 2s-electron is promoted to the 2p orbital.
One 2s-electron is promoted to the 3s orbital.
One 2s-electron is promoted to the 2d orbital.
The 2s-electron remains in the same orbital.
questions.solution: In the excited state of a Be atom, one of the 2s-electrons is promoted to a vacant 2p orbital to account for its bivalency.

questions.q: How is the bond length defined for covalent bonds?
options: The distance between the outermost electrons of two atoms
The distance between the nuclei of two atoms in a molecule
The distance between the innermost electrons of two atoms
The distance between the valence electrons of two atoms
questions.solution: Bond length for covalent bonds is defined as the distance between the nuclei of two atoms in a molecule.

questions.q: What is the result of sharing two pairs of electrons between two atoms?
questions.solution: When two pairs of electrons are shared between two atoms, it results in a double covalent bond.

questions.q: How is electron affinity defined?
options: The energy change when an atom loses an electron
The energy change when an atom gains an electron
The energy change when a molecule forms a covalent bond
The energy change when an ion is formed from an atom
questions.solution: The electron affinity is the negative of the energy change accompanying electron gain, which means it represents the energy change when an atom gains an electron.

questions.q: How is the dipole moment of a polyatomic molecule calculated when it has multiple bonds?

By adding up the individual dipole moments as vectors
By subtracting the individual dipole moments
By multiplying the individual dipole moments

questions.q: What happens to the electrons of a covalent bond when nitrogen, oxygen, or fluorine is attached to a hydrogen atom?

questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: What is the purpose of the Molecular Orbital (MO) Theory?
options: To understand the electronic configuration of elements
questions.solution: The Molecular Orbital (MO) Theory is one of the theories used to predict molecular shapes.

questions.q: Which type of atoms are considered in bond enthalpy calculations?
questions.solution: The bond enthalpy calculations consider atoms in a gaseous state.

questions.q: In which physical state is the magnitude of H-bonding minimum?
questions.solution: The magnitude of H-bonding is minimum in the gaseous state.

questions.q: Why do atoms combine?

questions.q: How is hydrogen bond defined?

It is the attractive force between two hydrogen atoms.
It is the attractive force between a hydrogen atom and an electronegative atom of another molecule.
It is the repulsive force between two hydrogen atoms.

questions.q: What is the electronic configuration of carbon in its ground state?

questions.q: What effect does the extent of distortion (polarization) of the anion have on the percent covalent character of an ionic bond?

It decreases the percent covalent character.
It has no effect on the percent covalent character.
It reverses the percent covalent character.

questions.q: What is the primary factor that determines the shape of a molecule, according to the VSEPR theory?
options: The number of valence shell electron pairs around the central atom
The size of the central atom
The electronegativity of the central atom
questions.solution: According to the VSEPR theory, the shape of a molecule depends on the number of valence shell electron pairs (bonded or non-bonded) around the central atom.

questions.q: What is the minimum requirement for each combining atom in Lewis dot structures?
options: To contribute at least one proton to the shared pair
To contribute at least one neutron to the shared pair
To contribute at least one electron to the shared pair
To contribute at least one electron and one proton to the shared pair

questions.q: What is the result of hybridisation in terms of orbital energies and shape?
options: Formation of orbitals with equivalent energies and shape
questions.solution: Hybridisation results in the formation of new orbitals with equivalent energies and shape.

questions.q: Why are molecular orbitals difficult to obtain directly from the Schrödinger wave equation?
options: Because the Schrödinger wave equation cannot be solved for systems with multiple electrons
Because they involve spin properties of electrons
questions.solution: The molecular orbitals are difficult to obtain directly from the Schrödinger wave equation because it cannot be solved for systems containing more than one electron.

questions.q: Which type of hydrogen bond is commonly observed in water molecules?
questions.solution: Water molecules commonly exhibit intermolecular hydrogen bonds.

questions.q: What is the theoretical limitation of the VSEPR theory?
options: It cannot explain the geometry of simple molecules.
It is based on quantum mechanical principles.
questions.solution: The VSEPR theory gives the geometry of simple molecules but theoretically does not explain them.

questions.q: Why does the second O – H bond in polyatomic molecules like ethanol and water show a difference in energy compared to the first O – H bond?
options: Due to changes in the chemical environment
Due to differences in the number of bonds
questions.solution: The second O – H bond in polyatomic molecules like ethanol and water shows a difference in energy because of changes in the chemical environment.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: What is the specific goal of atoms in chemical bonding, as per the electronic theory?
options: To gain or lose all their electrons
To have a full octet of electrons in their valence shells
To have no electrons in their valence shells
To share their electrons with other atoms
questions.solution: The goal of atoms in chemical bonding, according to the electronic theory, is to have an octet in their valence shells.

questions.q: Which types of orbitals are present in the third period elements?
questions.solution: The elements in the third period contain d orbitals in addition to s and p orbitals.

questions.q: What is the value of the bond dissociation enthalpy for the dissociation of HCl into H and Cl atoms?
questions.solution: The value of the bond  dissociation enthalpy (∆aH⊖) as 431.0 kJ mol-1 for the dissociation of HCl into H and Cl atoms.

questions.q: In chemistry, how is the presence of dipole moment represented on a Lewis structure?
options: A small arrow with a cross on the positive end
A small arrow with a cross on the negative end
A crossed arrow with a cross on the positive end
A crossed arrow with a cross on the negative end

questions.q: What kind of forces exist between ions of like charge?
questions.solution: Repulsive forces exist between ions of like charge.

questions.q: What factors does the formation of ionic compounds primarily depend upon?
options: The atomic number of the elements
The ease of formation of positive and negative ions
questions.solution: The formation of ionic compounds primarily depends upon the ease of formation of positive and negative ions.

questions.q: How does the formation of a negative ion occur?
options: Addition of protons to the neutral atom
Addition of neutrons to the neutral atom
Removal of electron(s) from the neutral atom
Addition of electron(s) to the neutral atom
questions.solution: The formation of a negative ion involves the addition of electron(s) to the neutral atom.

questions.q: What shape do the orbitals formed due to sidewise overlapping have in the case of a pi (π) bond?

questions.q: How can you determine the group valence of an element based on Lewis symbols?
options: By counting the number of protons
By adding the number of valence electrons and inner shell electrons
By subtracting the atomic number from the number of dots
By either counting the number of dots or calculating 8 minus the number of dots

questions.q: What equation is used to derive atomic orbitals in wave mechanics?
questions.solution: The atomic orbitals are obtained from the solution of Schrödinger wave equation.

questions.q: What is a formal charge in the context of polyatomic molecules or ions?
options: The actual charge on an atom within the molecule
The difference between the number of valence electrons in an isolated atom and the number assigned in the Lewis structure
The total charge of the molecule or ion
The electronegativity of an atom in a molecule
questions.solution: The formal charge of an atom in a polyatomic molecule or ion as the difference between the number of valence electrons of that atom in an isolated state and the number of electrons assigned to that atom in the Lewis structure.

questions.q: What effect does the polarizing power of the cation have on the percent covalent character of an ionic bond?
options: It increases the percent covalent character.
It decreases the percent covalent character.
It has no effect on the percent covalent character.
It reverses the percent covalent character.

questions.q: What is the relative orientation of the p orbitals involved in the pi (π) bond in ethene?

questions.q: What is the ultimate goal of combining atoms in Lewis dot structures?
options: To attain the configuration of noble gases
To attain the configuration of halogens
To attain the configuration of alkali metals
To attain the configuration of transition metals
questions.solution: The combining atoms attain the outer-shell noble gas configurations as a result of the sharing of electrons in Lewis dot structures.

questions.q: What aspect of atoms' valence shells does the theory proposed by Sidgwick and Powell focus on?
questions.solution: The theory proposed by Sidgwick and Powell is based on the repulsive interactions of the electron pairs in the valence shell of the atoms.

questions.q: Why is an average bond enthalpy used in the context of polyatomic molecules?

To account for differences in bond length
To account for variations in bond strength

questions.q: What factor primarily contributes to the stabilization of the crystal structure in ionic solids?
options: Energy released in the formation of the crystal lattice
Achieving an octet of electrons around the ionic species in the gaseous state
questions.solution: The crystal structure in ionic solids gets stabilized due to the energy released in the formation of the crystal lattice.

questions.q: What is the key concept that Lewis introduced to explain chemical bonding?
questions.solution: Lewis introduced the concept of electron sharing as a key concept to explain chemical bonding.

questions.q: In what state do ionic compounds exhibit orderly three-dimensional arrangements of cations and anions?
questions.solution: The crystalline state is the state in which ionic compounds exhibit orderly three-dimensional arrangements of cations and anions.

questions.q: What is the dipole moment of a nonpolar molecule?
options: Equal to the charge of the molecule
Double the charge of the molecule

questions.q: What important difference between lone pairs and bonding pairs of electrons did Nyholm and Gillespie explain?

Bonding pairs occupy more space than lone pairs.
Lone pairs are shared between two atoms.
Lone pairs have greater repulsion than bonding pairs.

questions.q: What type of forces are involved in the calculation of lattice enthalpy?

Only repulsive forces between ions of like charge
Both attractive forces between ions of opposite charges and repulsive forces between ions of like charge
questions.solution: The process of calculating lattice enthalpy involves both attractive forces between ions of opposite charges and repulsive forces between ions of like charge.

questions.q: What type of sigma bond is formed between carbon atoms in ethane?

When potential energy is at its minimum.
When the attractive force is less than the repulsive force.

questions.q: What does Lewis postulate about how atoms achieve a stable octet of electrons?

questions.q: What distinguishes the ammonium ion (NH4+) from most cations in ionic compounds?
options: It is composed of metallic elements.
It is composed of non-metallic elements.
It forms anions instead of cations.

questions.q: What is the typical source of anions in most ionic compounds?

questions.q: What is the implication of the statement, "Even in the case of a covalent bond between two hydrogen atoms, there is some ionic character"?
options: Covalent bonds are always purely covalent.
Hydrogen atoms cannot form covalent bonds.
Covalent bonds may have a small degree of ionic character.
Hydrogen atoms form exclusively ionic bonds.

questions.q: What type of bond is formed when two atoms share one electron pair?
questions.solution: When two atoms share one electron pair, they are joined by a single covalent bond.

questions.q: What is the basis of the octet rule?
questions.solution: The octet rule is based upon the chemical inertness of noble gases.

questions.q: What is the unit of bond dissociation enthalpy?
questions.solution: The unit of bond dissociation enthalpy is "kJ mol-1".

questions.q: Which noble gases combine with oxygen and fluorine to form compounds?
questions.solution: Noble gases like xenon and krypton combine with oxygen and fluorine to form compounds.

questions.q: Bond enthalpy is defined as the amount of energy required for what specific action?

Breaking one mole of bonds between two atoms
Changing the state of one mole of bonds

It measures the distance between valence electrons.

questions.q: How is the direction of the crossed arrow in chemistry related to the conventional direction of the dipole moment vector?

The crossed arrow points in the opposite direction to the dipole moment vector.
The crossed arrow has no relation to the dipole moment vector.
The crossed arrow is perpendicular to the dipole moment vector.

questions.q: What is the valence shell electronic configuration of nitrogen in the ground state?

Hybrid orbitals are used in bond formation.

questions.q: What term describes molecules and ions that have the same number of electrons?

3p orbitals have higher energy than 3d and 4s orbitals.
The energies of 3p and 4s orbitals are comparable.
The energies of 3p orbitals are significantly different from those of 4s orbitals.

questions.q: What term is used to describe compounds of elements in and beyond the third period with more than eight valence electrons around the central atom?

questions.q: How does the VSEPR theory treat resonance structures when determining molecular shape?
options: It considers only one resonance structure.
It averages the shapes of all resonance structures.
It treats each resonance structure separately.
It applies the VSEPR model to any resonance structure.

questions.q: What happens to the energy of the bonding orbital compared to the parent orbitals?
questions.solution: The energy of the bonding orbital is lowered compared to the parent orbitals.

questions.q: What is the relationship between the canonical structures and the resonance hybrid in the concept of resonance?

The canonical structures are completely different from the resonance hybrid.
The resonance hybrid is a combination of the canonical structures.
The resonance hybrid is used to generate the canonical structures.

questions.q: What is the bond between two carbon atoms in an ethene molecule?

By comparing the energy levels of orbitals
By evaluating the ratio of N<sub>b</sub> to N<sub>a</sub>
By analyzing the color of the molecule
questions.solution: The molecule stability is determined by comparing the number of electrons in bonding orbitals (N<sub>b</sub>) to the number in antibonding orbitals (N<sub>a</sub>).

questions.q: What does the VSEPR Theory primarily focus on?
options: Predicting the energy levels of electrons
Determining the electronic configuration of atoms
Predicting the geometry of molecules based on electron pair repulsions
Determining the polarity of chemical bonds

questions.q: How many sp2 hybrid orbitals of each carbon atom in ethene are used to form sigma bonds with hydrogen atoms?

To determine the energy levels of electrons

Reason (R) : Lattice enthalpy is a direct measure of the electrostatic forces of repulsion among the constituent ions in an ionic solid.

options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct, but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct, but (R) is correct
questions.solution:
Assertion (A): Higher lattice enthalpy leads to greater stability of ionic compounds. This statement is correct. Lattice enthalpy is the energy released when gaseous ions combine to form one mole of a solid ionic compound. A more negative (higher in magnitude) lattice enthalpy signifies a stronger attraction between ions and thus a more stable ionic compound.
Reason (R): Lattice enthalpy is a direct measure of the electrostatic forces of repulsion among the constituent ions in an ionic solid. This statement is incorrect. Lattice enthalpy is a measure of the strong electrostatic forces of attraction between the oppositely charged ions in the crystal lattice, not repulsion.
Therefore, Assertion (A) is correct, but the Reason (R) is incorrect. The correct option is (3).

b) $\mathrm{LiF}$ is more covalent than $\mathrm{KF}$
c) $\mathrm{SnCl}_2$ is more covalent than $\mathrm{SnCl}_4$
questions.solution:
- a) The total number of sigma bonds present in benzene is 12. This is correct. Benzene (\(\mathrm{C}_6 \mathrm{H}_6\)) is a hexagonal ring with six carbon atoms. Each carbon atom is bonded to two other carbon atoms and one hydrogen atom.
- There are \(\mathrm{6 C - C}\) sigma bonds within the ring.
- There are \(\mathrm{6} \mathrm{C}\)-H sigma bonds on the periphery.
- Total sigma bonds \(=6+6=12\).
- b) LiF is more covalent than KF. This is incorrect. According to Fajan's rules, a smaller cation and a larger anion lead to greater covalent character. Both \(\mathrm{Li}^{+}\) and \(\mathrm{K}^{+}\) are from Group 1, but \(L i^{+}\)is much smaller than \(K^{+}\). A smaller cation has a higher polarizing power, which increases the covalent character. Therefore, LiF is more covalent than KF. The statement says the opposite, making it incorrect.
- c) \(\mathrm{SnCl}_2\) is more covalent than \(\mathrm{SnCl}_4\). This is incorrect. A higher oxidation state of the central metal atom increases its polarizing power and thus increases the covalent character of the bond. In SnCl2, the oxidation state of tin is + 2, while in SnCl4, it is + 4. Therefore, SnCl4 is more covalent than \(\mathrm{SnCl}_2\). The statement says the opposite, making it incorrect.

- b) The p orbitals in ethene are parallel. The two unhybridized p-orbitals on the \(s p^2\) hybridized carbon atoms are parallel to each other, allowing for side-by-side overlap to form the pi bond.
- c) Propyne has 6 sigma bonds. The structure (\(C H_3-C \equiv C H\)) contains three \(\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{H}\) bonds, one \(\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{C}\) single bond, and one \(\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{C}\) bond within the triple bond, and one \(\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{H}\) bond, for a total of 6 sigma bonds.
- d) The electromeric effect is a temporary effect. It only occurs in the presence of an attacking reagent.
Thus, the correct statements are a, b, and c.

questions.solution:
Dipole moment of \(\mathrm{NH}_3\) is more than \(\mathrm{NF}_3\)
True \(\checkmark\)
\(\mathrm{NH}_3\) and \(\mathrm{NF}_3\) both have a pyramidal structure due to the lone pair on nitrogen.
In \(\mathrm{NH}_3\), the bond dipoles \((\mathrm{N}-\mathrm{H})\) and the lone pair dipole reinforce each other, leading to a higher dipole moment.
In \(\mathrm{NF}_3\), the highly electronegative fluorine atoms pull electron density away from nitrogen, opposing the lone pair dipole, resulting in a lower dipole moment.
\(\mathrm{SF}_4\) is square planar
False \(\times\)
\(\mathrm{SF}_4\) has a seesaw shape due to the presence of one lone pair on sulfur (\(\mathrm{A} \mathrm{X}_4 \mathrm{E}\) type in VSEPR theory).
Square planar geometry would require \(\mathrm{AX}_4 \mathrm{E}_2\), which is not the case here.
\(\mathrm{SnCl}_4\) is more covalent than \(\mathrm{SnCl}_{\mathbf{2}}\)
True \(\checkmark\) (Based on Fajan's Rule)
\(\mathrm{Sn}^{4+}\) in \(\mathrm{SnCl}_4\) has a higher charge density than \(\mathrm{Sn}^{2 +}\) in \(\mathrm{SnCl}_2\), leading to greater polarization of the \(\mathrm{Cl}^{-}\)anions.
More polarization means higher covalent character, making \(\mathrm{SnCl}_4\) more covalent than \(\mathrm{SnCl}_2\).
In \(\mathrm{I}_{\mathrm{2}} \mathrm{SO}_4\), sulfur has expanded octet
True \(\checkmark\)
In \(\mathrm{l}_2 \mathrm{SO}_4\) (Iodine sulfate), sulfur forms more than four bonds, which means it uses d-orbitals to accommodate additional bonding electrons.
This leads to an expanded octet.

ii. The dipole moment of chloroform is zero.
iii. Covalent bond character in $\mathrm{NaCl}$ is more compared to $\mathrm{CuCl}$.
questions.solution:
Only statement (i) is correct.
- i. The dipole moment of \(\mathrm{NH}_3\) is higher than the dipole moment of \(\mathrm{NF}_3\). This is correct. In \(\mathrm{NH}_3\), the bond dipoles of the three \(\mathrm{N}-\mathrm{H}\) bonds and the lone pair on nitrogen all point in the same general direction, adding up to a larger net dipole moment. In \(N F_3\), the bond dipoles of the three N-F bonds point towards the highly electronegative fluorine atoms, while the lone pair dipole points away. These dipoles oppose each other, resulting in a much smaller net dipole moment.
- if. The dipole moment of chloroform is zero. This is incorrect. Chloroform (\(\mathrm{CHCl}_3\)) is a tetrahedral molecule with three highly electronegative chlorine atoms and one less electronegative hydrogen atom. The bond dipoles do not cancel each other out, resulting in a significant net dipole moment.
- iii. Covalent bond character in NaCl is more compared to CuCl . This is incorrect. According to Fajan's rules, a smaller cation with a pseudo-noble gas configuration (like \(C u^{+}\)) has a greater polarizing power than a cation with a noble gas configuration (like \(\mathrm{Na}^{+}\)). This increased polarizing power leads to a greater covalent character. Therefore, CuCl is more covalent than NaCl.

questions.solution:
The molecular orbital σ formed by the addition of atomic orbitals is called the bonding molecular orbital while the molecular orbital σ* formed by the subtraction of atomic orbital is called antibonding molecular orbital.

The electron density in a bonding molecular orbital is located between the nuclei of the bonded atoms because of which the repulsion between the nuclei is very less while in case of an antibonding molecular orbital, most of the electron density is located away from the space between the nuclei. Infact, there is a nodal plane (on which the electron density is zero) between the nuclei and hence the repulsion between the nuclei is high.
